transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I'm here because I just can't seem to sit still. Like, whether I'm in my college classes or working in the radiology suite, I feel like I'm crawling out of my skin if I have to stay in one place. I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, but it's not working. I always end up pacing around, constantly shifting in my seat, or just finding any excuse I can to get up and move. It's really starting to become a problem.
Are you currently taking any prescription medications?
No, I'm not taking any prescription medications. I haven't been on anything at all.
When you feel that need to move, are you experiencing a lot of racing, worried thoughts in your mind?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel worried or anxious when it happens. My mind isn't really racing with thoughts like that. It's more just... a physical feeling, you know? My body just feels like it has to move, even if my head is completely calm.
Have you felt this constant need to move your body like this since you were a child, or is this something that only started more recently?

It's definitely been since I was a kid. Um, my parents actually still talk about my elementary school conferences. The teachers always said I was constantly out of my seat, calling out, or just rushing ahead to do things before they even finished giving the directions. So, yeah, this was happening way before middle school. It's not just something that started recently with my radiology training.
